questions.question: The projected statement of comprehensive income forecasts:
options: PROFIT — expected income earned against expenses incurred, on the accrual basis

questions.question: Depreciation appears in:
options: The projected income statement ONLY — no money moves, so it never enters the cash budget

questions.question: Items appearing in the cash budget ONLY include:
options: Capital contributed, drawings, loan receipts and repayments, fixed asset purchases and VAT paid over

questions.question: The classification test for every line in a question is:
options: Is the amount large or small?
Does it move MONEY this month (cash budget), or earn income / consume value this month (projected income statement), or both?

questions.question: With credit sales of R150 000 in February and 50% settling in the following month less 5% discount, March collects from February:
options: R71 250 — 50% of R150 000, less the 5% discount

questions.question: March's collections from debtors draw on:
options: THREE different months' credit sales — February, January and December

questions.question: The settlement discount is applied:
options: To the whole month's credit sales
To all collections in the month
ONLY to the portion that earns it — the group settling in the first month

questions.question: The 5% of credit sales never collected:
options: Reduces the cash budget's receipts line
Appears as a payment in the cash budget
Is added to next month's collections
Never appears in the cash budget — it appears in the projected income statement as bad debts

subtopics.title: Building the Cash Budget and the Projected Income Statement

questions.question: The cash budget's arithmetic chain runs:
options: Receipts less payments = surplus or deficit; plus opening balance = closing balance, which becomes next month's opening
Sales less cost of sales = gross profit
Opening stock plus purchases less closing stock

questions.question: In the projected income statement, sales are recorded:
options: In FULL — cash and credit alike — in the month of sale

questions.question: A forecast closing bank balance that turns negative is:
options: Impossible if the business is profitable
A forecast OVERDRAFT — the single most useful warning a business can receive
A reason to stop trading immediately

questions.question: A good answer to "how can a business forecast profit and a cash deficit in the same month?" must:
options: Say one is cash and one is profit
State that the budget is wrong
NAME the timing difference and the specific items causing it — credit sales collected later, stock paid earlier, an asset bought for cash

questions.question: A variance is stated properly by giving:
options: The item, both figures, the difference in rand and percentage, and whether it is favourable or unfavourable
The budgeted figure and nothing else

questions.question: A FAVOURABLE expense variance is not automatically good news because:
options: Advertising far below budget may explain the sales shortfall beside it, and maintenance not done becomes next year's breakdown
It means the budget was too low

questions.question: Presenting a projected income statement known to be unachievable, to obtain a loan, is:
options: MISREPRESENTATION — a fraud on the lender

questions.question: What makes a budget a control rather than a wish is:
options: The COMPARISON afterwards — actual against budget every month, with material variances explained

questions.question: The cousin who did R8 000 of hair but holds R4 000 shows that:
options: Earning well and having money are two different, both-honest answers about the same month

questions.question: Drawings, buying a bakkie and repaying a loan appear:
options: In the CASH BUDGET — they move money even though they are not profit or loss items

questions.question: Depreciation goes only in the profit forecast because:
options: It is too small to budget
The bakkie is wearing out this month, but no rand left the account for that wearing
It is a form of drawings

subtopics.title: Working Out What Will Actually Arrive

questions.question: Money arriving in March comes from:
options: Half of February's credit sales, thirty percent of January's, fifteen percent of December's — three months landing in one
An equal share of every month

questions.question: With December, January and February credit sales of R108 000, R120 000 and R150 000, March's collection from debtors is:
The grid — sales down the side, arrival months across — exists because:
options: Three different months' sales land in one month's bank account, and holding that in your head crosses lines

questions.question: You cannot budget to receive the five percent that never comes because:
options: It is collected the following year
It is paid by the supplier
You cannot budget to receive money you will never get — it belongs in the profit forecast as bad debts

subtopics.title: Profitable and Broke at the Same Time

questions.question: The shop's best-ever month can empty its bank account because:
options: Stock was paid for last month, wages went out this month, a bakkie was bought for cash, and the credit customers have not paid yet

questions.question: "Profit tells you whether the business deserves to survive; cash tells you..."
options: Whether it WILL — a business can survive a bad profit month but not a payday with an empty account

questions.question: Seeing the shortfall in advance gives the owner cheap options such as:
options: Delaying the bakkie, arranging an overdraft calmly, tightening collection terms, or negotiating longer supplier payment

questions.question: Budgets get "dressed up" when:
options: Sales forecasts are inflated to obtain finance, or expenses padded to hide later overspending
